review_policy: Original explanatory notes checked against the linked upstream references. Examples are illustrative, not automatically executed or runtime-validated on a target. Check the installed version's help for differences.

guides.scope: Nmap reference guide: version detection and port selection; installed builds may differ
guides.description: Use Nmap to turn a known host into an inventory of reachable services. It actively sends network probes; an open port is a starting point for investigation, not proof of a vulnerability. Choose a small, authorized scope before enabling version detection.

guides.scope: Upstream tcpdump manual; capture permissions and interface support depend on the host
guides.description: Use tcpdump when you need a small terminal-native packet capture or a quick look at an existing pcap. It can read saved traffic without a live capture interface. Capturing traffic may require privileges and can collect sensitive content.

guides.scope: TShark manual: offline capture-file reading and Wireshark display filters
guides.description: Wireshark is the graphical protocol explorer; TShark is its command-line companion. Use TShark for reproducible offline inspection and Wireshark for interactive protocol trees. Capture filters and display filters are different languages.

guides.scope: GNU Binutils readelf reference; examples inspect existing ELF files
guides.description: Use readelf to identify an ELF file's architecture, entry point, sections and symbols without intentionally executing that file. A stripped executable may have little symbol information. The utility is part of Binutils, not a separately named package on Arch.

guides.scope: Samba smbclient 4.25 reference; server authentication and policy vary
guides.description: Use smbclient to discover accessible SMB shares and browse a selected share with an FTP-like interface. Share discovery does not imply permission to read every file. Let the client prompt for a password instead of placing credentials in shell history.

guides.scope: Binwalk v3 README: signature inspection and help; no cross-version extraction flags assumed
guides.description: Use Binwalk for an initial map of recognizable data embedded in firmware or another binary blob. A signature match is evidence to investigate, not proof that a complete filesystem can be extracted. Version 3 is a Rust rewrite and older extraction recipes may not apply.

guides.scope: Gobuster v3 upstream README (3.8.x): directory mode and explicit help
guides.description: Use Gobuster to test candidate web paths from a wordlist on an authorized application. It makes active requests and can create significant load. A successful response or a 403 is a lead to inspect, not proof of a vulnerability.

guides.scope: Osmocom rtl_test.c and rtl_sdr.c usage references; RTL-SDR hardware required
guides.description: The RTL-SDR utilities separate hardware checks from raw radio capture. rtl_test checks sample delivery; rtl_sdr records raw interleaved I/Q data. Neither command automatically identifies or decodes an arbitrary radio protocol.
